data.title: Mid-Level Frontend Engineer
data.fitReason: Three years of React and TypeScript in a demanding fintech context with measurable performance outcomes (40% load time reduction) and junior mentorship align almost perfectly with mid-level frontend expectations. Trading dashboard complexity signals above-average component architecture and state management depth, directly matching what most product companies expect at this level.

data.title: Mid-Level React Developer
data.fitReason: Deep React and TypeScript specialisation with production fintech exposure is a direct match for React-focused product teams. The Tailwind and CI/CD familiarity further reduces onboarding friction. Slightly lower than the broader frontend engineer role because some companies at this title expect narrower scope without the performance engineering or mentorship signal.

data.title: Mid-Level Fullstack Engineer
data.fitReason: Node.js/Fastify API work with PostgreSQL demonstrates genuine fullstack initiative, and the strong frontend foundation means the candidate brings more frontend depth than most fullstack hires at this level. The main limitation is that backend exposure is approximately one year and lacks evidence of scale, so fit depends heavily on whether the role is frontend-weighted fullstack versus balanced.

data.title: Frontend Engineer – Fintech
data.fitReason: Direct domain match. Built React and TypeScript trading dashboards with real-time data handling in a live fintech environment, which is exactly the experience fintech-specific job postings screen for. Performance engineering credentials in a high-stakes financial product further differentiate this candidate from generic frontend applicants.

data.title: UI Engineer – Design Systems
data.fitReason: Stated interest in design systems combined with Tailwind proficiency and React component depth provides a credible foundation. However, the candidate has no portfolio, open-source contributions, or documented design system work, which are typically screening requirements for this specialisation. Fit improves significantly if they can demonstrate even one internal design system contribution.

data.title: Frontend Performance Engineer
data.fitReason: The 40% load time reduction on trading dashboards is a direct and rare credential for a role centred on performance optimisation. Most candidates at this level cannot quantify impact this concretely. The gap is limited public evidence of tooling knowledge (profilers, Core Web Vitals, bundle analysis) beyond the single outcome, which niche performance roles typically require candidates to articulate in depth.

data.title: JavaScript Engineer – Node.js
data.fitReason: TypeScript proficiency and Node.js/Fastify API experience make this a plausible application, and the PostgreSQL exposure helps. However, backend depth is roughly one year in an internal tooling context, which falls short of the two-plus years of production backend ownership most Node.js-focused roles expect. Best suited for companies that value frontend-to-backend career trajectory or need frontend-aware backend engineers.

data.title: Frontend Tech Lead
data.fitReason: Junior mentorship and strong delivery ownership are early lead signals, but formal tech lead roles typically require cross-team technical influence, architectural decision history, and broader organisational visibility. This candidate could be competitive at smaller startups or companies willing to grow someone into the lead track, but would be screened out at larger organisations requiring five-plus years with documented leadership scope.

data.title: Developer Experience Engineer
data.fitReason: Stated interest in developer experience aligns with the role direction, and CI/CD familiarity and TypeScript depth are relevant foundations. However, DevEx roles typically require documented toolchain ownership, internal platform contributions, or open-source presence — none of which are evidenced in this profile. The interest is credible but unsubstantiated, making this a stretch application without portfolio support.

data.title: Software Engineer – Product (Frontend-Leaning)
data.fitReason: Product-focused engineering roles at mid-sized tech companies often prioritise React and TypeScript depth, fullstack flexibility, and delivery ownership over pure specialisation — all areas where this candidate is strong. The combination of frontend performance credentials, backend initiative, and mentorship makes this candidate well-rounded for collaborative product teams that value generalist execution over narrow expertise.
